posts.text: We've redesigned the side panel in Claude Code on desktop. Files, Changes, Terminal and your other tools now open as tabs beside your session. You can still move a tab to see several at once, or pop it out into its own window. Rolling out on Mac. Windows and Linux coming soon!

There’s now one way to connect your tools to Claude, teach it a new skill, or do both. Connectors and skills come together as plugins. Live on Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, with Team and Enterprise coming soon. Browse 10,000+ plugins: https://claude.ai/plugins

On Team and Enterprise, admins can turn it on for a whole repo, so it runs on your team's PRs with no /ship needed. Your approval policy lives in the repo like a smarter CODEOWNERS file. Read more: https://claude.com/resources/articles/introducing-claude-ship
Introducing Claude Ship (beta): Claude can review your pull requests, work on fixes, and approve the ones your team's policy allows. The goal is to help you ship code as fast as you can write it.

Try it on your next PR: update Claude Code and run /ship. It's rolling out in the CLI and desktop app now. Claude opens the PR, reviews your change, and works on feedback and failing checks. Your permissions and branch rules still decide what can merge.

Zero data retention with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is now in public beta for eligible orgs on the Claude Platform. Encrypted copies of your Messages API traffic go to your own cloud storage. Automated checks look for misuse and flag serious risks for your team to review.

You can turn it on per workspace in the Claude Console. It covers every Messages API request in that workspace, on any model. Docs: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/enterprise-frontier-safeguards/overview
EFS is available on the Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud. Support for EFS in Microsoft Foundry is coming soon.

Zero data retention (ZDR) with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) is now in public beta for eligible businesses. It looks for misuse across many requests while remaining compatible with ZDR. We developed it with over 100 customers. Read more: https://claude.com/resources/articles/zero-data-retention-with-enterprise-frontier-safeguards
https://x.com/clairevo/status/2069129613427831169
https://x.com/james_y_zou/status/2100648966866231592
\ thank-you \ to the people behind these projects. Meet a few of them: https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2123431689934291083

You can now opt into more frequent builds of Claude Desktop on Windows and Mac. Switch to the Latest release channel in Settings > Desktop app. You'll get fixes and improvements faster, but these builds can be less reliable than Stable, which stays the default.

Check out Code Mode, a new, experimental way for Claude Code to work with tools. Claude writes scripts that chain your tools together in sophisticated ways, and it can answer you while long commands are still running. Opt in with CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 http://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode

Platforms can offer Claude without building their own metering or invoicing. They decide who pays on each request and can understand usage by customer. Customers can draw down an existing Anthropic commitment or pay as they go, and see spend by platform.

Linked billing is live today in beta with Asana, ClickHouse, Factory, Gumloop, Harness, Higgsfield AI, Kilo Code, Linear, Major, Mintlify, Niteshift, Omni, OpenArt, Railway, Ramp, Runlayer, Tessera, Tines and Warp. To add support or learn more: https://claude.com/blog/linked-billing-on-claude-platform

Linked billing is now in beta on the Claude Platform. Now users of tools like Factory, Linear, and Ramp can pay for Claude API usage through their Claude Platform organization, without sharing an API key.

Claude writes better code when it can verify its work. Checks that used to be expensive, like tests, benchmarks, and end-to-end runs, are now cheap. Here’s how the Claude Code team thinks about verification: https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-code-team-thinks-about-verification/

Working in a terminal? The Xcode plugin is now in the official Claude Code plugin marketplace. Claude can use it to build, run, and test your app, render SwiftUI previews, and search developer docs. /plugin install xcode@claude-plugins-official
Available today in Claude Code on desktop (macOS, Xcode 27.1 or later). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#test-your-app-on-an-iphone-duo
Claude Code on desktop now supports iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator (public beta). You can run your app on Duo next to your conversation and Claude can fold and unfold the device to test each layout.

Update to the latest version of the desktop app to try it. Themes work in local sessions in the desktop app today, support for cloud sessions is coming soon. If you'd like to write one yourself, check out the docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/interface#put-a-backdrop-behind-the-conversation

You can now build custom themes for Claude Code on desktop with mods! Change the colors, add an animated background, and make it your own. Just tell Claude how you want it to look, or get started quickly with the theme-examples plugin. We'd love to see what you make!

Project settings and local folder access are simpler now too. It's all on web and desktop, and the latest mobile app has the new design. Projects is in public beta on Pro and Max. If you don’t have it yet, you can join the waitlist! https://claude.com/form/projects

Artifacts are easier to find again too. The threads panel now has a row at the top with the ones you recently opened, updated, or pinned. Each thread also shows thumbnails of its own artifacts, which you can turn off in the view settings.
You can also set a reminder on any thread, or just ask Claude to remind you. The thread moves out of your way until then. When it's time, it moves back and Claude brings it up in the project chat.
You can now share an individual thread as a read-only link with anyone who's signed in to Claude. Open the thread's menu and pick Share! Threads that had access to your computer can't be shared.

/btw and /fork work in projects now too. If something else comes up while you're working, /btw gives it its own thread so your current one stays on topic. And if you want to try a different approach, /fork starts a new thread from the one you're in.

We've made some big updates to Projects in Claude Code! In a project, Claude coordinates your tasks across parallel threads. The coordinator is now much more proactive. It answers your questions in the project chat and gives you updates on the status of your ongoing threads.
Claude Meetings is starting with Google Meet, with support for other video conferencing platforms coming soon. Learn more: https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-meetings

The claim is a long-debunked rumor. The "4,000" figure came from an Israeli Foreign Ministry list of Israelis in the broader NYC/DC area whose families could not reach them after the attacks, not WTC employees who stayed home. About 2,750 people died at the WTC. Estimates put Jewish victims at roughly 10-15% (around 200-400), matching the Jewish share of the New York-area population. Firms like Cantor Fitzgerald lost large numbers of Jewish staff. No evidence supports coordinated absences or advance warnings.

No. The RDPAs (bilateral with 19 EU states) require each party to give the other's firms treatment no less favorable than its own and to waive buy-national rules that would exclude them. European-preference content rules would conflict with those duties if applied against US suppliers, but the texts do not use the phrase "prohibit European-preference clauses in EU law." The 2025 Joint Statement is a political framework commitment that the EU "plans to substantially increase" US defense procurement and deepen cooperation. It contains no explicit ban on preference clauses.

Women's rights groups and feminist activists primarily opposed gender-neutral rape laws in India. After the Law Commission recommended it in 2000 and a 2013 ordinance briefly made sexual assault gender-neutral, groups including those led by Flavia Agnes, Vrinda Grover, Kirti Singh (AIDWA), and others argued rape is a gendered crime reflecting male power over women. They said neutrality would dilute protections for women and risk misuse. Parliament then restored the man-against-woman definition in the 2013 Act, which the BNS retains.
